newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Japan no easy victim for terrorists - Hashimoto.
newsitem.headline: Japan no easy victim for terrorists - Hashimoto.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Monday his country was no pushover for terrorists.

"Our country had been described generally as a country that is weak in the face of terrorism and that when threatened was always willing to pay," he told a parliamentary dinner in Canberra, six days after Peruvian troops ended a four-month siege at the Japanese embassy in Lima.

Hashimoto, on a visit to Australia and New Zealand, said Japan respected the judgement of Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori, who sent in Peruvian army and navy commandos in a daring military strike last Tuesday, rescuing all but one of 72 hostages.
"But we also showed this time that when hostages are taken we do not just pay, follow the demands of the terrorists and expose Japanese lives to crisis," he said through an interpreter.

Throughout the crisis Japan repeatedly called for a peaceful settlement and analysts said Hashimoto, who was not asked to authorise the rescue, may have been privately relieved that he did not need to take the decision.
Fujimori's soldiers killed all 14 of the Peruvian rebels on April 22, beginning the raid by detonating explosives in a tunnel under the hostage-takers' regular soccer game.
Earlier on Monday Japanese media reported Fujimori saying he had not consulted Tokyo before ordering the raid because Japan thought the embassy was impregnable.
"Japan's call for a peaceful resolution was idealistic and did not offer concrete suggestions," he said.
Immediately after the raid Hashimoto at first appeared irritated by Peru's failure to warn him, but he later said he understood the decision.
The day after the raid Hashimoto said Fujimori had explained he had not warned Japan because it had been a "very delicate situation".
